title: Prompt groove experiments
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal lab for small, composable prompt templates + few-shot mixes. Not polished — iterative notes to capture odd behaviors and cheap mitigation ideas.

Top hypotheses to test:
1) Short templated cues that establish role + target format reduce hallucination on numerical outputs more than adding more exemplars.
2) Mixing heterogeneous few-shots (different tones) increases variance; cluster-by-style before sampling reduces mode collapse.
3) Lightweight negative examples (showing what NOT to do) sometimes reduce confident hallucinations.

Sketches / experiments done (fast logs):
A - Numeric-precision template (10-shot)
Prompt skeleton:
"""You are a concise analyst. Output only JSON with keys: {answer, rationale_score (0-1)}.
Example:
Q: "Estimate yearly churn given monthly retention 0.92"
A: {"answer": "9.6%", "rationale_score": "0.8"}
"""
Result: model followed format but crept on "rationale_score" semantics. When reduced to 3 shots, answer precision stayed similar but rationale_score became noisy.

B - Tone-cluster few-shot sampler
Plan: pre-tag exemplars as {formal, playful, terse}. For a given prompt, pick exemplars matching user-specified tone.
Observation: matching tone helps for style but sometimes removes useful structural exemplars; hybrid approach (2 structural + 1 tone) better.

C - Negative examples (antipatterns)
Include 1 example of "bad answer" demonstrating hallucination and short note: "Don't do this".
Observation: decreased confident hallucinations in 2/5 trials, but introduced confounding phrase tokens. Use sparingly.

Failure cases seen recently:
- Context bleed: long system+conversation leads to earlier exemplars being effectively ignored after 6k tokens. Suspect attention scaling / position bias.
- Shot mismatch: exemplar uses list-of-steps but target asks for paragraph -> model attempts list+paragraph hybrid.
- Overfit to formatting tokens: strict JSON schema tokens can cause empty fields when uncertain.

Small mitigation checklist (cheap):
- Pre-validate exemplar format (automated) and only include exemplars whose output length is within +/-50% of target expected length.
- Add short clarifying suffix to prompt: "If unsure, answer: \"I don't know\"." This reduces confident hallucinations but increases conservative outputs.
- For numeric answers, append a micro-instruction: "Show 1-line working or say 'est'"; reduces spuriously precise numbers.

Ideas to try next (backlog):
- Rolling exemplar window: for long conversations, resample exemplars from most recent 1k tokens rather than full history.
- Soft-negative regularization: include a 1-line note in system prompt discouraging confident fabrication rather than an explicit negative example.
- Few-shot curriculum: start with 1 exemplar, then request chain-of-thought for one exemplar only, then ask for final answer — measure latency vs accuracy.

Quick artifacts to attach when I formalize: small eval harness (200 prompts) bucketed by prompt-type, and a cheap metrics sheet: hallucination-rate, fmt-compliance, token-overhead.

Notes-to-self:
- Save useful exemplars to GH prompt-registry under tag "groove-v1".
- Share anecdotal failures in #prompt-lab and ask for examples where negative-example trick backfired.
- When writing up, include short AB test vs baseline (no exemplars) with same token budget.

Recent run outputs (examples):
1) Q: "Forecast monthly revenue growth (3 months) based on MRR=12500, growth trend +5% p/mo."
A (model): "{\"answer\": \"15,000\", \"rationale_score\": \"0.9\"}" -> check arithmetic, seems off.
2) Q: "List 3 safe rephrasing options for: 'The system will always be available'"
A: model produced 5 items; formatting drift.

End.
